summary: Prelaunch review of notes/sim10_perlmutter_baseline_20261115 at baeb8a6 (base 410ebba1c, adapter files only). Most of the plan is implemented in code: an exact 11-case schedule adding up to 5400 s; srun --mpi=cray_shasta with explicit task counts and a Cray MPICH check; 3,3,7 / 3,3,7,7,7,7 masks with no SMT siblings; helper ranks masked from CUDA; GPU sharing allowed only for the S 4BD/1GPU bridge (enforced in plan, runner and audit); hash-checked frozen calibration; an owner-scoped count2 allowlisted cold-cache gate run after setup; remote traffic labelled unverified; byte, range-digest, drain, publication and weakref gates; 4 GiB headroom checked by in-process samples, NVML and the audit; exports retained on shared scratch with no-overwrite directories and fsync; independent per-bin readback hashing; loop timing kept separate from export/reference; per-step deadline guards; no retry or automatic promotion. Two problems block the first job. (1) The Slurm deadline is read from a local-time scontrol EndTime but parsed as UTC, so on a node using Pacific time campaign.py would stop at once with 'Allocation deadline elapsed' and use up the single allowed attempt; the host test hides this because it builds a UTC EndTime. (2) The required explicit granted UUID/PCI mapping is only checked for distinct PCI counts; each BD's actual PCI bus ID is never compared with the nvidia-smi UUID-to-PCI inventory. Non-blocking: an undocumented change to the vendored adapter.py, missing host tests for ECC readback, affinity, storage and prepare, host-test evidence not tied to this commit, lock-failure status handling, an unpinned calibration manifest, and time limits not backed by per-profile evidence. The stale 'awaiting authorization' status files were not counted against the review, as instructed. GPU execution, the full-shape memory fit, full reference cost and runtime results remain pending and are not claimed.

findings.evidence: run.sbatch:17 runs scontrol show job before clean_exec.py sets TZ=UTC, so EndTime is printed in node local time. campaign.py:33 parses it with replace(tzinfo=utc). With Pacific local time the deadline is 8 h early, so line 34 fails 'Allocation deadline elapsed' before any work and uses up the only attempt. test_port.py:27 builds a UTC EndTime, which hides the bug.
findings.requested_change: Get the deadline in a timezone-safe way: run TZ=UTC scontrol show job in run.sbatch, or use squeue -h -o %e under TZ=UTC, or SLURM_JOB_END_TIME epoch if available. Add a host test with a non-UTC local EndTime, and check that the deadline is within the 5400 s TimeLimit.

findings.evidence: Acceptance requires explicit granted UUID/PCI mapping, and PLAN.md:65 says UUIDs are validated against actual PCI IDs. runner.py:125 records deviceGetPCIBusId, and campaign.py:90 stores the nvidia-smi uuid,pci.bus_id inventory as text. Only distinct-PCI counts are checked (runner.py:263, audit.py:47). Nothing compares each BD's PCI with the inventory PCI for its assigned UUID.
findings.requested_change: Parse the inventory into a UUID-to-PCI map (normalize bus-ID format). In the runner and in the independent audit, require each BD's PCI to equal map[assigned UUID]. Add a corruption test.

findings.evidence: source-origins.json records origin sha d0a41a58... while host-checks.json records e7d70068... for the vendored adapter.py. port_sources.py does not edit adapter.py, and limitations.md documents only the test_reference.py fixture change. Lines 19-20 show an ad hoc 'import os' and a SIM10_PR_SOURCE calibration path, but the full extent of the change cannot be confirmed.
findings.requested_change: Add the adapter edit to port_sources.py as an exact replacement (or a recorded diff) and document it in limitations.md. Pin the loaded jungfrau_calibration.py source hash as a runtime check.

findings.evidence: The 63 host tests cover only staging-receipt corruptions and the plan/placement/allocation basics. They do not cover the ECC audit branch (manifest mismatch, bin size/shape/sha readback, non-empty bin 99, counts), support.affinity / select_affinity (3,3,7 prefix, overlap, SMT), the storage.cache allowlist rejection, prepare.py / verify_bundle tamper detection, runstep timeout kill, or a non-UTC deadline.
findings.requested_change: Add host tests for these paths, at least ECC readback corruption, affinity mapping rejection, cache allowlist rejection and bundle tamper detection. Rerun the native host suite.

findings.evidence: The host checks ran from /global/u2/.../lcls2_worktree/features/psana2-gpu with no commit recorded. source_hashes covers only *.py, omitting runtime.sh, run.sbatch, expected-native.json and other bundled JSON.
findings.requested_change: Record the git HEAD and clean status in checks.json, hash every bundled file type, and rerun from the exact reviewed commit.

findings.evidence: status.json is written as 'running' at line 78, but the non-blocking flock at line 82 is outside the try block. If the lock is held, the job exits with status left as 'running', not 'failed'.
findings.requested_change: Take the lock inside the try block, or before writing the running status, so that a lock conflict is recorded as failed.

findings.evidence: reference.load_constants checks arrays against PACKAGE/calibration/manifest.json, but the bundle's external pins include only PACKAGE.json, not the manifest. At runtime nothing re-checks the manifest that the frozen-calibration gate depends on.
findings.requested_change: Add PACKAGE/calibration/manifest.json (and the constant files, or their manifest hashes) to bundle['external'] so verify_bundle checks them.

findings.evidence: The 600 s ECC acceptance limit must cover serial, exhaustive rank-0 CPU references for 1003 events, per-BD full-pixel CPU-v3 checks and a 12.5 GiB fsynced export. The 240 s limit must cover 1BD/batch50 100k staging plus setup and cold-cache conditioning. No per-profile measurement supports either, and the reference-cost probe runs after the acceptance cases.
findings.requested_change: Record the basis for these limits or accept the stated risk explicitly. Consider running the reference-cost probe before the acceptance cases, and record a separate setup/conditioning timing so a timeout can be attributed.
